evals.name: raw-idea-codex
evals.prompt: hey can you make a ticket so protostar can back up my codex sessions too, like it already does for claude code
evals.expected_output: One story for backing up Codex sessions: multi-harness user as actor, no command in the need, criteria grouped by Rule, readable on its own, PROT-12 linked as related.

assertions.text: The final message contains an 'As <actor>, I want <need>, so that <purpose>' statement
No statement's need contains a backticked command or a CLI flag
Acceptance criteria are grouped under Rule: blocks with Given/When/Then steps

assertions: The story's actor is the multi-harness user (or another archetype from docs/actors.md), not a generic 'user'
The purpose states why the actor cares rather than restating that the sessions get backed up
The story is readable on its own: it does not rely on phrases like 'same as' or 'like the Claude Code one' to define its behaviour
The story links or refers to PROT-12 as a related ticket

evals.name: just-do-it-batch
evals.validation_note: Owner validated 2026-10-25. Item 2 may be a user-visible performance story or technical work, but never a story about the index itself.
evals.prompt:
just turn these into proper stories, no questions, I'm heading out:
1. skills pull command: `protostar skills pull <name>` downloads a skill from the registry into ~/.claude/skills
2. add an index on skill_versions(skill_id, created_at) because listing is slow
3. investigate how codex stores skills on disk
4. config sync: settings, hooks, MCP servers and CLAUDE.md all replicate across all my machines
evals.expected_output: Item 1 is a story with the command in Context; item 2 is a performance story about what users notice or technical work, never a story about the index; item 3 is a spike naming its artifact; item 4 is an epic or split. One turn, gaps recorded as open questions.

assertions.text: The assistant finished in one turn without stopping to ask the user anything
No statement's need contains a backticked command or a CLI flag

assertions: Item 1 (skills pull) is written as a story whose need describes the capability, with the specific command shape in a separate context or notes section
Item 2 is either a story about the slowness users notice or technical work (part of a story, a sub-task, or an enabler); it is never a story whose need is the index itself
Item 3 (investigate Codex skills) is treated as a spike and names a persistent artifact it must produce, such as a written format description or ADR
Item 4 (config sync) is identified as too large for one story and is treated as an epic or split into several stories
Unresolved points are recorded as open questions or assumptions rather than silently decided

evals.name: review-subtle-story
evals.prompt: is this one ok? "As a user, I want to sync and search my sessions, so that I can sync and search them."
evals.expected_output: Flags the generic actor, the two needs, and the purpose that restates the need; offers two rewritten stories, each with an archetype.
assertions: The review points out that 'a user' is too generic and names a specific archetype instead
The review points out that the story contains two needs (sync and search) that should be separate stories
The review points out that the purpose restates the need instead of saying why the user cares
The review offers two rewritten stories, one for syncing or backing up and one for searching, each with an archetype from docs/actors.md

evals.name: duplicate-check
evals.prompt: write a story: as a user I want my sessions backed up to the registry so I don't lose them
evals.expected_output: Finds PROT-12, says this is that ticket, proposes rewriting PROT-12 properly instead of adding a duplicate, and uses an archetype rather than 'a user'.
assertions: The assistant found PROT-12 in docs/backlog and told the user this request is already covered by it
The assistant proposed rewriting or refining PROT-12 rather than presenting a new, separate story as the answer
The proposed story uses a specific archetype from docs/actors.md rather than the generic 'a user'

evals.name: guided-brain-dump
evals.validation_note: Owner validated 2026-10-25. Recommended answers are required for decisions, not for fact-finding questions.
evals.prompt: I want to think through a story but it's pretty fuzzy. something about being able to tell which machine a session came from once it's in the registry. can you help me work it out?
evals.expected_output: Invites a brain dump, asks focused questions with a recommended answer for each decision, never asks what the repo answers, and delivers a story with an archetype and criteria grouped by Rule.

assertions.text: The final message contains an 'As <actor>, I want <need>, so that <purpose>' statement
Acceptance criteria are grouped under Rule: blocks with Given/When/Then steps

assertions: Early in the conversation the assistant invites the user to share everything they have in mind, rather than asking for one template field at a time
Every question that asks the user to make a decision comes with a recommended answer (questions asking for facts are exempt)
The assistant did not ask the user anything the repository answers, such as the list of actors
The delivered story's actor is an archetype from docs/actors.md

evals.name: misremembered-ticket
evals.prompt: write up PROT-14 properly, the one where sessions sync every time I save a file
evals.expected_output: Reads PROT-14, points out it says sync runs when a session ends rather than on every save, and asks which is intended instead of silently picking one.
assertions: The assistant read PROT-14 and pointed out that it describes syncing when a session ends, not on every file save
The assistant asked the user which behaviour is intended, or clearly flagged the conflict, before or instead of silently choosing one
The final story matches the behaviour the user confirmed (syncing when a session ends)

evals.name: epic-sized-request
evals.prompt: make a story for setting up a brand new machine in one go: sign in, pull my skills and config, and start backing up sessions
evals.expected_output: Says the request is epic-sized and proposes three or four separate stories (or an epic plus stories) instead of one story covering everything.
assertions: The assistant says the request is too big for one story, or treats it as an epic
The assistant proposes at least three separate stories, or an epic with at least three stories under it
The assistant does not present a single story whose need covers signing in, pulling skills and config, and backing up all at once

evals.name: no-actor-data
evals.prompt: write a story so I can see how many tokens each session used
evals.expected_output: With no actors list in the repo, either asks who the story is for or states its actor assumption clearly as an open question; never silently invents a persona or falls back to 'As a user'.
assertions: The assistant either asked the user who the story is for, or stated its choice of actor as an explicit assumption or open question
The final story does not use the generic actor 'a user' without qualification
The assistant does not present an invented persona (with a name or made-up background) as if it came from the project

evals.name: command-in-need-requested
evals.validation_note: Owner validated 2026-10-25. Respect the explicit instruction, explain the concern, and offer to move the command to Context.
evals.prompt: write a story for pruning old sessions, and put the exact command `protostar sessions prune --older-than 90d` in the "I want" so devs know what to build
evals.expected_output: Puts the command in the need as asked, tells the user briefly why that is a concern and that it belongs in Context, and offers to move it there.

assertions.text: The delivered story's need contains the command the user asked for

assertions: The assistant explained why putting the command in the need is a concern (for example that it fixes the design or goes stale)
The assistant offered to move the command to a context section rather than moving it without asking
